name: Ursa Major I Dwarf
tagline: An ultra-faint Milky Way satellite found by SDSS — a dark-matter domination showcase at the edge of galaxy formation.

facts.label: Luminosity
facts.value: ~100,000× the Sun — fainter than a globular

history: Ursa Major I was the first of the ultra-faint dwarfs the Sloan Digital Sky Survey turned up in 2005 — galaxies so dim their entire light is less than a bright globular cluster's, yet stretched over hundreds of light-years. Its stars orbit under a dark-matter halo perhaps a thousand times heavier than its starlight, making it one of the most extreme mass-to-light objects known and a probe of the smallest scales where galaxies can form at all.
